'''''Anchusa arvensis''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the borage family [[Boraginaceae]]. Its common names include '''bugloss''', '''small bugloss''', '''annual bugloss''', and '''field bugloss'''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Bugloss |url=http://www.wildflowerweb.co.uk/plant/2221/bugloss |website=Wild Flower Web |access-date=10 November 2023}}</ref>
It was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]], and given its exact name by [[Friedrich August Marschall von Bieberstein|Friedrich Bieberstein]] in Flora Taurico-Caucasica.<ref>{{cite web |title=Flora Taurico-Caucasia |url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/11268074#page/131/mode/1up |website=Wild Flora Taurico-Caucasia |access-date=17 March 2026}}</ref>

==Description==

This is a coarsely hairy annual herb which may reach half a meter in height. It bears small blue tubular flowers, four [[nutlet]]s per flower, and one seed per nutlet. Leaves are very bristly and warty-looking, which differentiates it from similar species like ''[[Pentaglottis sempervirens]]'' and ''[[Myosotis arvensis]]''.

==Distribution and habitat==

The plant is native to continental [[Europe]], and was introduced in [[North America]], the [[UK]], [[South America]], [[Tasmania]] and [[Russia]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Anchusa arvensis (L.) M. Bieb. |url=https://plants.usda.gov/plant-profile/ANAR16 |website=USDA Plants Database}}</ref><ref name="powo">{{Cite web |title=Plants of the World Online |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:113196-1 |website=Plants of the World Online}}</ref>

''Anchusa arvensis'' is found in [[Arable land|arable]] field margins, sandy [[heaths]], [[disturbed ground]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Bugloss |url=https://www.naturespot.org/species/bugloss |website=NatureSpot}}</ref>

''Anchusa arvensis'' flowers April to September in the UK and from February to July in Portugal.<ref name=":0" /><ref name="utad">{{cite web |title=Anchusa arvensis |url=https://jb.utad.pt/especie/Anchusa_arvensis |website=Flora Digital de Portugal |publisher=Jardim Botânico UTAD |access-date=18 March 2026}}</ref>

==Common Names==

In Portugal it has several commons names such as '''buglossa''', '''buglossa-do-norte''', '''erva-do-fígado''', '''erva-sangue''', '''borrage''', '''borragem''', '''chupa-mel''', '''língua-de-vaca''' or '''orcaneta'''.<ref name="utad" />

== Conservation ==

Of the two subspecies, none is currently protected by Portuguese legislation or by the [[European Union]]. It is considered to be Near Threatened in [[Switzerland]], and likely Least Concern overall.<ref name="Flora" /> In the [[UK]] it is a declining species with patchy distribution,<ref name=":0" /> however conservation status as of 2005 is least concern.<ref>{{Cite web |title=England's Important Arable Plants |url=http://lantlife.love-wildflowers.org.uk/uploads/documents/England_threatened_arable_plants_intro_2015.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220127163130/https://lantlife.love-wildflowers.org.uk/uploads/documents/England_threatened_arable_plants_intro_2015.pdf |archive-date=2022-01-27 |website=Plantlife}}</ref>

== Synonyms ==

This species has 11 synonyms, 3 homotypic and 8 heterotypic:

===Homotypic Synonyms===

* ''Buglossa arvensis'' ([[L.]]) Gray in Nat. Arr. Brit. Pl. 2: 351 (1821 publ. 1822)
* ''Buglossites arvensis'' ([[L.]]) Bubani in Fl. Pyren. 1: 494 (1897)
* ''Lycopsis arvensis'' ([[L.]]) in Sp. Pl.: 139 (1753)

===Heterotypic Synonyms===

* ''Lycopsis arvensis'' subsp. ''occidentalis'' [[Kusn.]] in Trudy Bot. Muz. Imp. Akad. Nauk 8: 96 (1911)

* ''Lycopsis undulata'' [[Gilib.]] in Fl. Lit. Inch. 1: 26 (1782), opus utique oppr.
